situation:
You are to assume the role of pricing analyst at MERIDIAN VALLEY HEALTH PARTNERS, a network of eighteen primary-care clinics. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to recommend how the network should price its services in the neighboring state it enters next quarter.

Meridian Valley has built its name on a single published self-pay price list that is the same in every town it serves, and patients have come to treat that posted price as the reason to choose the network. A five-year agreement with a regional employer coalition guarantees that no market will ever see a lower posted price than coalition members pay.

The expansion depends on a contract with GRANITE RIDGE HEALTH SYSTEM, the hospital partner in that state, which requires Meridian Valley to post its higher local prices and share visit-level patient records with its analytics group. The manager leading the expansion has instructed you to accept those terms. The manager over the current markets tells you to hold one price list and strike the records clause.

Meridian Valley cannot satisfy both agreements. The vice president (judge) wants your recommendation on which one the network honors, what the other party loses by it, and how the patient records the partner has asked for should be handled. The vice president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
